title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-29
content:
2026-03-03 / quick morning notes + TODO

Context:
- Follow-up day after last night's rolling kernel update on on-prem gpu nodes (rack-3). Saw 2 nodes fail to come back (nvlink driver mismatch). Ticket INFRA-4321 opened.
- Hosted cluster autoscaler triggered burst at 02:14 UTC due to a sudden spike in short-lived chat requests (model: redwood-chat-medium). Need to verify batching config.

Top of inbox / blockers:
- INFRA-4321: stuck on pending driver rollback for rack-3-node-07. Miguel checking HSM mounting side-effects. If rollback not possible, schedule controlled reprovision tonight 00:00-01:00 UTC.
- Quota increase request for GCP GPUs (a100) still pending — INFRA-4330. Finance-approved but cloud quota team needs more details. Prepare usage CSV and per-customer SLA notes.

Today TODO (priority order):
1) reprovision rack-3-node-07 if driver rollback not resolved by EOD. Steps: cordon -> drain -> reprovision image (img-gpu-2026-02) -> validate nvidia-smi & nvlink -> uncordon.
   - Commands: kubectl cordon rack-3-node-07; kubectl drain rack-3-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   - Post-check: kubectl get nodes -o wide; ssh root@rack-3-node-07 tail -n 200 /var/log/nvidia-installer.log
2) Investigate autoscaler spike root cause: pull prometheus query around request rate and pod startup latency (query: increase(redwood_api_request_total[5m]) / increase(redwood_api_request_total[1m]) — rough). Check batching config for redwood-chat-medium route.
3) Prep materials for quota increase: attach per-region projected GPU-hours for next 90 days + commit plan for Dedicated customers. Use estimate spreadsheet template (link in linked_artifacts).
4) Add small runbook snippet for kernel-update rollback to runbook page: confluence page id 9876543. Include commands and common failure modes (nvlink, DKMS, HSM mounts).
5) Follow up with SRE on network flaps observed 2026-03-02 23:45 UTC (spike in TCP retransmits on ib0). Might be related to top-of-rack switch firmware. Slack: #sre-networking.

Monitoring / quick checks to run now:
- GPU node health (all zones): kubectl get nodes -l accelerator=nvidia -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,CPU:.status.capacity.cpu,GPU:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp
- GPU util: PromQL: avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization[5m]) by (node) — look for nodes < 10% but >0% with many pods (hot-warm imbalance).
- Check prefix cache hit-rate in redis cluster: redis_keyspace_hits / redis_keyspace_misses for prefix-cache-*

Notes / observations:
- Batch sizes for redwood-chat-medium look conservative (max_tokens_per_batch set to 64). For short-chat workloads median seq_len ~ 48; safe to bump to 96 for tail latency bound? Need canary.
- On-prem reprovision window: prefer 00:00-02:00 UTC to minimize impact for EU customers. Schedule canary on rack-3-node-02 first.
- Consider temporary routing policy to route non-SLA traffic to lower-cost quantized model if autoscaler keeps triggering. TODO: check routing policy config in repo infra/routing/policies.yaml (PR #512).

Housekeeping / follow-ups:
- Add test to release pipeline that validates kernel-driver pairing for the Google image builder. Ticket: INFRA-4399 (create).
- Sync with Samir tomorrow 10:00 PT on Dedicated capacity forecasts and commit thresholds.
- Clean up old scratchpads weekly (remind self).

Random notes to self:
- If nvlink errors persist, try older nvidia driver 535.x instead of 540.x; record results in INFRA-4321.
- Customer alert post (if reprovision causes brief outage): brief note: "We've scheduled a maintenance window to reprovision GPU node to fix driver issue, expected <10 minutes impact to <1% of inference traffic." Draft in docs/incident-templates.

Quick links / commands stash:
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference --field-selector=status.phase=Pending
- nvidia-smi topo --matrix
- ssh root@rack-3-node-07 "journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200"

End of notes.

-- Ava
